question: Does the MACS1931 surplus-image problem recur across the 26 other observed source families, and which P0554 components most often predict missing, exact, demagnified-surplus, or potentially observable-surplus image multiplicity?

evaluation.systems: all five raw clusters used in the interaction experiment
evaluation.families: all 27 observed source families, including families without held-out images
evaluation.potentially_observable_surplus_threshold: absolute magnification at least 0.25 times the faintest assigned root in that formula-family
evaluation.exact_multiplicity: number of global roots equals number of published images
evaluation.demagnified_only_surplus: root count exceeds published count but no unassigned root crosses the frozen relative-magnification threshold
evaluation.potentially_observable_surplus: at least one unassigned root crosses the frozen relative-magnification threshold
evaluation.missing_multiplicity: fewer global roots than published images

interpretation_rules.primary_comparison: family-level counts of missing, exact, demagnified-only-surplus, and potentially-observable-surplus classifications
interpretation_rules.route_warning: a route variant is disfavored if it increases potentially observable surplus families without improving matched image-position RMS

claim_limits: All five clusters and formulas are spent exploratory evidence.
Published multiple-image catalogs can omit central, demagnified, obscured, or unrecognized images.
Relative magnification from the simplified lens is a screening proxy, not a calibrated detection completeness function.
The finite interlaced root search can miss very small attraction basins or roots outside 120 arcseconds.
Many archived geometry fits touch nuisance bounds and the lens omits registered gas and diffuse ICL.
